Subject: Crescent: bespoke retention & deletion — high level Qs

Mina — thanks for the intro last week. Our security and compliance team asked me to capture a few concrete questions so we can get an Order Form amendment in place ahead of the pilot. High level: Crescent needs a bespoke retention policy for three data classes (PHI extracts, telemetry/logs, and prompt/artifact traces). Specific asks below: 

- Can Redwood guarantee a maximum retention window for prompt/artifact traces (we prefer 90 days), and for PHI extracts (we may need 365 days for care continuity) as a configurable Order Form field?
- What does “deletion” mean operationally across deployments (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private)? Do you provide a certified deletion report?
- How long after termination will data be irrevocably wiped from backups/snaps and on-device persistent storage? We need an upper bound for our contract (Crescent policy requires certified destruction within 60 days of contract termination unless otherwise agreed).
- Are audit logs and proof-of-deletion (hash manifests, KMS envelope records, job ids) available to customers via the Console or as an exported artifact?

Attached: Crescent data class matrix (CSV) to map classes -> examples. Can we schedule a short call (30 min) next week to align on the proposed wording?

Thanks,
Emma

Emma — thanks for the clear list and the matrix. I pulled together a concise proposal for how we typically represent bespoke retention in an Order Form amendment and the operational expectations across deployment modes. Summary below; attached is a draft Order Form amendment and our internal eviction playbook for reference.

Proposal (order-of-magnitude / negotiable):
- Retention by data class (Order Form configurable):
  • Prompt/artifact traces: default 90 days (customer can set 30–365 days)
  • Telemetry/logs (operational): default 180 days; can be restricted to 90 days for high-sensitivity customers
  • PHI extracts / customer-provided PII datasets: default up to 365 days (can be shortened to 90 days on request)
- Deletion semantics and evidence: 
  • Deletion = removal from active serving layer, persistent object stores, and all standard snapshots.
  • For hosted and dedicated: backups and cold snapshots are subject to a staged purge (see timelines below) and final deletion is accompanied by an exportable audit manifest (job id, object list, deletion timestamps, SHA256 manifests), plus a signed Certificate of Deletion if requested.
  • For Private (VPC/on-prem): Redwood will provide guidance and an exportable deletion manifest; physical/host-level wipe may be customer-managed depending on hosting model — we can add an explicit clause to the Order Form if you require Redwood-managed on-prem wipes.
- Termination windows (defaults, can be tailored in Order Form):
  • Active data purge starts within 7 calendar days of contract termination request.
  • Standard staged purge completes within 45 calendar days.
  • Final irrevocable wipe of backups/snapshots within 90 calendar days, unless longer retention is explicitly purchased in Order Form.
- Proofs & access: audit manifests are downloadable from the Console; we additionally provide a signed Certificate of Deletion (PDF) and an audit bundle (~JSON/CSV) via a secure S3 share or encrypted Drive export.

Operational notes / mitigations:
- We use staggered eviction to avoid reliability impact: in-memory KV cache (purge within 24–72 hours), serving caches (purge 7–30 days based on SLA tier), long-term object store (30–90 days depending on class).
- If Crescent requires a stricter upper bound (e.g., final irrevocable wipe within 60 days), we can include that in the Order Form as a premium commitment with related fees and an SLA credit schedule.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick 30-minute sync to agree which data classes map to which retention buckets (30 min).
2) Redwood to send a redlined Order Form amendment with explicit clauses for: retention window per class, staged purge timeline, certificate delivery, and a failure-remediation SLA.
3) Crescent to confirm whether you want Redwood-managed on-prem wipes if you pursue Private.

I've attached the draft amendment and a short playbook (redwood-data-eviction-playbook.pdf) that shows the purge workflow and evidence types. Would Monday 12/14 at 9am PT work for a sync?

Best,
Mina Haddad

Subject: Re: Crescent: bespoke retention & deletion — technical clarifications

Emma / Mina — quick technical clarifications from the serving/runtime side that should be reflected in any Order Form/Annex: 

- KV and prefix caches: these are ephemeral by design; we can guarantee eviction within 72 hours for prompt traces, but for availability reasons we recommend 24–72 hours depending on traffic patterns.
- Snapshots & backups: object-store snapshots are immutable; final purge requires an overwrite/remove operation and execution of a deletion job which produces the audit manifest. For customers on Dedicated, we maintain separate snapshot retention policies per pool; those are configurable and must be included in the Order Form.
- Hardware/wipe for Private: if Crescent wants Redwood to coordinate physical disk scrubbing for on-prem appliances, add a clause for "Redwood-managed hardware sanitization" — turnaround 30–60 days depending on logistics. We will provide NIST 800-88 or equivalent certificate language.
- Evidence format: we can deliver: deletion_job_id, list_of_object_paths (compressed), deletion_timestamps (ISO8601), sha256_manifests, kms_key_id + envelope metadata, and a signed certificate. Recommend calling out format and retention of the audit bundle (e.g., keep deletion certificates for 2 years) in the Order Form.

I'll join the sync if you want to go into the runtime specifics. Also flagged that if Crescent needs a 60-day final wipe commitment, that will likely require the higher SLA tier and a backup retention carveout fee.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
